summary: All checklist items pass. The old color-class test (funnel-handle--<kind> assertions) was replaced — not left behind with now-false assertions, and not silently deleted. The replacement test is value-based and load-bearing: it asserts the exact ordered output-handle ids [next, btn:0, btn:1, timeout] via data-handle-id, verifies monochrome (no old per-kind classes), checks the four ordered labels [Далі, A, B, Таймаут], asserts exactly one card-target with funnel-handle--card-target class, and asserts no input dot. The start-node sub-block asserts one output (id=entry, label=Вхід) and no target — this is regression coverage for the entry path. Handle-id regression coverage is preserved: the typed-output-handles test (line 145) still keys on next/btn:0/btn:1/timeout/entry via data-test selectors matching the old ids (the connect path depends on these ids and they are explicitly called out as UNCHANGED in the implementation). The truncation test is load-bearing: it constructs a label longer than 16 chars, finds the element by endsWith('…') guard, and asserts the exact sliced value — removing the truncate() logic would produce an un-truncated label and the .slice(0,16)+'…' equality would fail. required-keys.spec.ts now enumerates outputNext and outputTimeout (lines 104-105), and both locales enforce non-empty values via the NON_EMPTY_REQUIRED_KEYS filter (the filter includes all funnels.canvas.* keys). No pointer-drag test pretends to cover the drop interaction — the test comment at the top of the file explicitly defers live drag/zoom to user verification, and the whole-card droppable behavior (pointer-events toggling, isConnecting computed) is not asserted in any hollow way. No existing coverage was weakened: all pre-existing tests are present and unmodified in the final file.
